header: Generated by `python3 tools/design_basis.py --write` from the code. Do not edit it: change the code, then run that command.

items.name: Idea
items.moment: At the desk, in a chat with Claude: you say what you want the gadget to do.

items.name: Needs
items.moment: At the desk: you read the needs Claude wrote from your goal and agree or change them.

items.name: Parts
items.moment: At the desk: you pick a part for each need, the parts you own first.

items.name: Parts list
items.moment: At the desk: Claude writes the parts list from your picks. You wait.

items.name: Board files
items.moment: At the desk: spark builds the board files in seconds. You read what built and what was skipped.

items.name: Wiring
items.moment: At the bench, hands busy, the USB cable out: you wire one step at a time, often from a phone.

items.name: Firmware
items.moment: At the desk, in the chat: you say what the gadget does, and Claude writes the firmware.

items.name: Simulation
items.moment: At the desk: you run the simulation in your terminal and read whether it passed.

items.name: On the board
items.moment: At the bench, the board on USB: you run the deploy in your terminal and look at the board.

items.label: Write the firmware
items.tell: Write the firmware for this project's board.

items.label: Run the simulation
items.tell: Help me run the simulation of this project.

items.label: Look at the board
items.tell: Look at this project's board with me.

items.summary: Drop a need and its pick from .spark/needs.json, and release only the holds of the dropped pick.

with --apply only, move a part that one project holds to another: FROM keeps each need that picked it, with no pick, and TO picks it for NEED. Without --apply it writes nothing, and says what each project loses and what goes out of date
every record a project can build with, and where it comes from
one record, wherever it lives, and its CONFLICT lines: on verified facts a problem (exit 1), on unverified ones an assumption
every record a project can build with, against the contract
the signals these parts ask for, as assign_pins.py input
what nobody has checked about these parts, one assumption a fact
write a record to fill in, to the project's parts/ (refused when any layer holds the id)
ask every URL a record cites whether it answers
download the datasheets and images a record cites, into your store; never spark's library

find a DFRobot board's top view and dimension drawing on the maker's wiki page by its sku, keep them in your store and list them in the board's documents; it draws nothing, and a file the record keeps already is not fetched again
put a file you already have into your store; answers its documents entry, and with --part lists it in that record
keep a picture of a part (an SVG in its frame, see --picture-frame) and name it in the part's record as its picture for a view
the frame a part's picture is drawn on: an SVG in mm of its outline and its pads, from its record or its board's
read a datasheet page by page and stop where every --want fact is on a table row
find a kept document by every word, with no network, and every fact resting on it
catalog → the project's parts/, or the project's parts/ → the plugin's library
every record research has kept, chosen or not
what you own: each entry's key, label, count, the record it is, unsure, skip — 20 at a time
a spine step of a project starts now, in this Claude Code session — the cost line counts its transcript from here

set drawer entries from a JSON list in FILE (- for stdin): every write sets, never adds; with --project, an `is` may name a record in that project, such as one /spark:research just wrote; an entry may also say its about, description and tags
apply an importer's payload (FILE, or - for stdin) to the drawer: new entries, and counts by the re-import rule
set what a part does — a JSON [{does, what}] in FILE (- for stdin) — in the record's own home (--project picks the project's copy); never spark's library

fill what a record owes — a JSON object of the facts the chain reads, or `facts` entries {value, verified, source} by name (a bench result is verified true and its source says who, when and how; a text in it has its control characters turned into a space and is cut at 1000 characters, and a key with a control character is refused), or its about, description and tags, or a board's onboard LED or button level, `pin_roles` {onboard_led|onboard_button: {active_level: {value, verified, source}}} (a board of the project's own, merged role by role), or a board's joined pads, `joined_pads` {value: [[pad, pad], ...], verified, source, why_it_matters, cites} (the groups of pads its maker's schematic joins inside the board, each pad in header_order; written to physical.header.joined_pads of a board of the project's own, replaced as a whole), or what the sheet reads, `legs` {pin of pin_order: how to tell the leg apart} (merged leg by leg), `host_requirements` [the lines the host board must meet] (replaced as a whole, like tags) and `short_name`, what the steps call the part, in FILE (- for stdin) — in the record's own home (--project picks the project's copy); never spark's library

write a board's main features (chips, sockets, buttons, LEDs, holes, labels), measured in the pixels of the maker's top view that the record keeps, into its record in mm: scaled by the outline, turned so the USB end is at the bottom (never mirrored), checked against the record's pads and mounting holes; verified false, each with its source

Research one part record from ordered sources (P737): find the geometry gaps the chain needs, keep the documents a DFRobot module's wiki page lists, ask one question per gap that cites the kept drawing, and write the replies as facts.
Every board available to switch to.
every record in every layer and every drawer link: what owes facts, what is broken

what you own and what spark knows for a need, before researching: the words against what each record (parts and boards, every layer) or drawer entry does, its tags, names and text, owned first (word-overlap); --matcher name-contains for the names alone
a project's needs: what each does, its condition, its mark, its picks

each of a project's needs with the store's candidates: owned first, what each owes, each with its score and why; --matcher picks the matcher that ranks them; a board that serves a need through its own LED, button or display has `limits`, the sentences for what a passed run does not test of it, and so has a part whose record skips the simulation or names a stand-in

what one offer says of itself, for the chooser to read: a record's id or a drawer entry's key — about, description, tags, what it does, its names, power and size, each fact without its sources (the record's file holds them). --project reads the project's own records

the picks as the project's requirements.json: the board, and every part pick with a record — one that owes only its outline or its simulation is written with a warning, one that owes more is refused; a catalog one goes onto the shelf; what the file already holds stays; board_only when the board itself serves every need; it names each entry that spark wrote for a pick that is gone (data.unexplained), and removes them on the person's yes in --replies
the cost line: the picks, how many came from the store (known to spark before the project: its library, your store, your projects) and how many you own, and what the project's steps cost
set a project's needs from a JSON list in FILE (- for stdin): every write sets, never adds. A write that defines a need, or [], also notes the goal and the must lines

set what each need picks (NEED=ID: a record, or a drawer entry) and reserve what you own of it — never past what another project holds; what it notes is under `notes`: a board given a need that its own part serves says what a run does not test of the part, and the other choice; a part whose record skips the simulation or names a stand-in says so
The one thing that has to work: a module list in, a board that builds out.
Run every deterministic check and answer once.
Read the board on USB without changing it, compare it with the project's board record, and print a token (P219).
Put the flash image onto the board: one that a passed run names (P192), or, with --no-simulation, firmware/ (P337).
Let Claude run code on one board for a time limit: one yes typed in your own terminal (P253).
Say whether the board on USB has a live grant now: the check a later call makes (P253).
Run a short piece of code on the running board inside a grant, say whether the board ran it, and reset it (P247).
Run one line on the board on USB, and cure it once when its USB output died at power-on: the PO's bench tool (P251).
each board on USB with its deploys, the projects that keep it and its grants, from spark's store; it opens no port
register a project that is not spark's, once, so that its own tool records its deploys with bench.py record; it touches no board
record one deploy of a registered project in spark's store, for the board on USB; it opens no port and reads nothing from the board
keep the file grants/direct_flashing_disallowed in your store, at once and with no question
Say where a project stands, phase by phase from the idea to the deploy, and what each phase offers next (P825).
Write page.html in the project: each phase of the flow with a status word and a mark, and the project's pictures (P827).
Run the step the page asked for in .spark/page-request.json, a pick, the parts list or the build, only when spark offers it now and the project has not changed since the page was read (P829).

items.name: Perfboard
items.moment: At the bench with a soldering iron: the same circuit, soldered to last. Optional.

items.name: PCB
items.moment: At the desk: a board to order, once the breadboard works.

items.name: Case
items.moment: At the printer: a case for the board.
